headline: Computational methods infer spatial and developmental dynamics from single-cell data
label: Single Cell Computational Methods
summary: Generative, optimal transport and deep Gaussian process models now scale to million-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of spatial and temporal organization from single-cell and spatially resolved data. Several items address spatial transcriptomics directly: CODA aligns multiple slices in a shared latent space, SMURF assigns mRNAs to nuclei and unrolls tissue geometry, SOCS infers trajectories in time-series spatial data, and G-LATO infers spatially smooth latent gradients in liver and glioblastoma. Others extend the scope: Navigo learns developmental vector fields from a 12.4M-cell mouse embryo atlas with RNA kinetics, 3D-Omics-Flow reconstructs 3D single-cell organization from 2D proteomics sections, and ParTIpy scales archetypal analysis to millions of cells. What distinguishes these methods is scale and explicit dynamical or three-dimensional modeling, rather than a single shared architecture.
